title: Keyboard manager breaks 3 and 4 finger touch pad taps with certain remaps
author: Zeebins

judgment.rationale: The long-running thread now explains the mechanism: precision touchpad taps can be emitted as Win+Ctrl+Shift+F22/F24 shortcuts, and modifier remaps interfere with those synthetic sequences. Users provide reproducible workarounds that explicitly remap the gesture shortcuts.
evidence: The original Alt/Ctrl swap disables configured three- and four-finger tap actions.
Users identify Win+Ctrl+Shift+F22 and F24 as the gesture sequences.
Explicitly remapping those sequences back to mouse actions restores behavior for some users.
The problem affects current Surface hardware and other remapping tools, indicating a Windows synthetic-input interaction.
judgment.recommended_action: Queue a Keyboard Manager design for preserving precision-touchpad synthetic gesture sequences across modifier remaps.

fix_assessment.rationale: The mechanism and workaround are well grounded, but a safe rule for recognizing or exempting Windows gesture sequences requires code-level design.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve Windows precision-touchpad gesture shortcuts across modifier remaps
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Windows precision-touchpad taps are represented by Win+Ctrl+Shift+F22/F24 sequences, and Keyboard Manager modifier swaps rewrite or suppress those synthetic sequences before Windows converts them to the configured gesture action.
plan: Trace F22/F24 precision-touchpad sequences through the current Keyboard Manager hook and identify reliable injected-input metadata.
Preserve recognized Windows gesture sequences while retaining normal user-defined modifier remaps.
Add regression coverage for three- and four-finger taps with Ctrl/Alt and Caps Lock/Ctrl swaps.
verification: Configure three- and four-finger actions, apply the reported modifier swaps, and confirm both gesture actions and ordinary remaps work.
Verify ordinary user-generated F22/F24 shortcuts are not unintentionally exempted.

confidence.rationale: The public sequence and workaround are strong, but safely distinguishing OS gesture input from user shortcuts still requires hook-level inspection.

issue_context.summary: Keyboard Manager modifier swaps can break Windows precision-touchpad three- and four-finger tap sequences encoded with F22/F24 shortcuts.
known_information: Three-finger tap commonly maps through F22 and four-finger tap through F24 with Win/Ctrl/Shift modifiers.
Modifier remaps change or suppress these sequences.
Manual shortcut remaps can restore the intended mouse action.
inferences: Preserving OS-generated gesture sequences may require recognizing their synthetic pattern or source.
issue_context.analysis: The evidence has progressed beyond a generic old-version request; the remaining problem is a platform/input-policy design.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the current public issue body, labels, assignees, and up to the latest 20 public comments returned by GitHub.
Kept the existing dashboard read-only; no dashboard files were modified or published.

information_gaps.information: How Keyboard Manager can distinguish OS touchpad gesture sequences from user-generated shortcuts without breaking valid remaps.
information_gaps.why_needed: This is the safety boundary for any exemption.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Inspect current low-level hook metadata and confirm the supported policy.

actions.label: Approve preserve windows precision-touchpad gesture shortcuts across modifier remaps
actions.note: Approve/start the fork-side design workflow from this public-evidence fix plan. No upstream write occurs from this action.

actions.label: Reproduce Keyboard manager breaks 3 and 4 finger touch pad taps with certain remaps
actions.note: Maintainer-side reproduction reduces the recorded implementation uncertainty without asking the reporter to perform code investigation.

prerequisites: A Windows precision touchpad with configurable three- and four-finger tap actions.
steps: Configure actions for three- and four-finger taps.
Swap Left Alt and Left Ctrl in Keyboard Manager.
Repeat with the posted F22/F24 workaround for comparison.
reproduce.expected_result: Configured touchpad actions work while the modifier swap remains active.
reproduce.observed_result: The gesture actions stop working unless the synthetic F22/F24 shortcut is explicitly remapped.
